digest.component_or_area: Jira Reconciler — baseline arbitration and three-way merge
propositions: A local status change (reopen/un-claim) is silently reverted by the reconciler one pass after rebar's own outbound push of that field, because the baseline is advanced from the pre-push fetch snapshot rather than the post-push synced value.

The baseline-equals-local guard (_suppressed_by_inbound) has a false premise for exactly one pass after rebar pushes a status: the baseline retains the old value while local has been changed, so local==baseline incorrectly signals 'local is unchanged' and suppression fires.
Other fields written in the same window (e.g. description) survive because they are not equal to the stale baseline, so they are pushed outbound and inbound has no conflicting value to apply.

The defect exposes any local state-field change made between rebar's outbound push and the next pass's baseline advance, where the new local value equals the pre-push baseline; silent, with zero pass-level indication.

Per-mutation success must gate the baseline advance, not the pass exit code, because status transitions can soft-fail (RuntimeError on illegal reverse transition) while the pass exits 0, and advancing a baseline for an unapplied push would mask genuine divergence rather than self-correct.
